messages:
Alex M.: hey team, asking for a short risk acceptance — we want to increase the pending key rotation window for the ephemeral worker KMS key from 1 day -> 7 days.

Alex M.: reason: a recent OpenSSL patch (CVE-2026-3141) needs image rebuilds. Rolling keys now would force all workers to re-auth at once and spike our auth DB + cause many failed jobs during customer migrations.

Priya K.: can you paste the exact compensating controls + timeline you propose?

Alex M.: planned controls:
- enable detailed CloudTrail for KMS + increase retention to 90d
- SIEM alert on decrypt count spike (baseline + 3 sigma)
- restrict decrypt permissions to service principal only (least-privilege IAM)
- cap new token TTL to 30m for worker tokens
- sequential rotate plan after maintenance window

Alex M.: terraform snippet we intend to apply (short):
```
resource "aws_kms_key" "ephemeral" {
  pending_window_in_days = 7
  description = "ephemeral worker key - temporary window request"
}
```

Jen (DevSec): need a concise risk statement, owner, CVE details, and rollback criteria before I can sign off.

Alex M.: risk statement: delaying rotation increases exposure time for the KMS key material if an unknown compromise exists, but the practical exploit path requires access to our network and service principal creds. owner: Alex M. (infra) + Tim L. (auth).
CVE: CVE-2026-3141 — affects OpenSSL <1.3.0, CVSS 7.1, exploitability moderate.
rollback criteria: revert `pending_window_in_days` to 1 and run an immediate rotation; or manual rotation earlier if SIEM detects anomalous decrypts or unexpected auth failures.
request window: 7 days starting now.

Maria S.: from oncall perspective — if we extend window we MUST increase CloudTrail retention and set SIEM alerts. i'll own the alert creation and monitor for the window.

Jen (DevSec): also require: Confluence runbook linked to the risk acceptance doc, explicit IAM policy diff in the PR, and a short post-mortem checklist in case we observe suspicious activity.

Tim L.: auth notes: rotating causes workers to re-request tokens which spikes DB. if we hold rotation we avoid immediate churn. i'll implement the token TTL cap to 30m for new tokens as additional mitigation. ETA ~2h.

deploy-bot: deploy request created: https://deploys.internal/requests/1234

Priya K.: quick question — how many services use this key? need a service list for the runbook.

Alex M.: services: api-ingress, worker-fanout, batch-runner, model-hotload, metrics-collector, sandbox-provisioner. Plan is sequential rotate per service after maintenance window.

Jen (DevSec): ok — I can provisionally approve for 7 days with the following conditions:
1) Confluence risk doc linked in the PR
2) CloudTrail retention = 90d
3) SIEM alert threshold created and tested
4) IAM restrict decrypt to service principal only and PR attached
5) Incident channel monitoring enabled and owner assigned

Jen (DevSec): will sign off in-thread once all conditions are met.

Tim L.: ACK — implementing TTL cap, IAM rule, and terraform change. will push a PR with the IAM diff and link the Confluence doc.

Maria S.: SIEM alert created and tested. increased CloudTrail retention. pinging here when verified.

Alex M.: thanks — i'll open the risk acceptance doc, attach terraform PR and Confluence runbook, and mark owners. requesting final security sign-off from @Jen (DevSec).

Jen (DevSec): :white_check_mark: approved. Conditions met and documentation attached in PR. Approval window = 7 days starting now. Re-evaluate sooner if SIEM fires or any anomalous decrypt activity observed.

Priya K.: noted and added to incident ops runbook. i'll monitor auth DB metrics during the window.

Alex M.: appreciate it. will close the risk doc after the 7-day window and include lessons learned.

(End of thread)"
